'''''Ismelia carinata''''', the '''tricolour chrysanthemum''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 |df=dmy-all}}</ref> '''tricolor daisy''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=GLCA5|taxon=Glebionis carinatum|accessdate=22 January 2016}}</ref> or '''annual chrysanthemum''', is an [[ornamental plant]] native to north Africa that is cultivated as a garden plant and grows as a weed in California.<ref>{{citation |chapter-url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250067006 |title=Flora of North America |chapter=''Ismelia'' |mode=cs1 |author=John L. Strother |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> It is the [[monotypic taxon|sole species]] in the genus '''''Ismelia'''''. It has been hybridized with related ''[[Argyranthemum]]'' species to create [[cultivar]]s of [[garden marguerite]]s.<ref name=FlorShawWats18>{{Citation |mode=cs1 |last1=Flores |first1=Anita |last2=Shaw |first2=Julian |last3=Watson |first3=John |date=2018 |title=Unpicking a daisy chain |journal=The Plantsman |series=New Series |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=238–243  |name-list-style=amp }}</ref>
